1981. The Chinese yuan and the Korean won enter the picture.
1997. Currency turmoil spreads across Asia. The Korean won loses much of its value.
September 1992. Speculators force the pound out of Europe's exchange-rate system.
June 2016. Britain votes to leave the European Union. The pound tumbles.
January 2015. Switzerland drops its cap on the franc, which jumps overnight.
June 1948. West Germany launches a new currency, the Deutsche Mark. Rates are fixed to the dollar, and the dollar to gold.
September 1985. Major economies coordinate to weaken the dollar. The yen strengthens in the years that follow.
January 1999. Eleven countries adopt the euro. The Deutsche Mark passes on its light.
1973. Fixed exchange rates collapse. Currencies begin to float freely.
2008. A global financial crisis sends shockwaves through currency markets.
August 1971. The dollar's link to gold breaks. A new monetary era begins.
Pinch a currency on the map or the chart to hear it alone. Pinch the hand panel to pause or jump in time.
March 2020. The pandemic sends investors rushing into dollars, for a few weeks.
1967. Britain devalues the pound from $2.80 to $2.40.
1969. The yen joins the stream, held at 360 yen to the dollar since 1949.
2022. US interest rates climb while Japan's stay near zero. The yen slides to its weakest in decades.
The full journey: every year from 1948 to today, in about four minutes. Pinch a currency to hear it alone.
Welcome aboard the Currency Time Machine!
I'm Tock, your guide to the history of money.
Pick a year, and we'll travel back to see who shaped the world, what happened, and how currencies changed.
Which year shall we visit? Turn the dial, or pick a famous year. Then press Start Travel.
